a: ‘For the accustomed security of Quraysh, their accustomed security…’: marvel at their being accustomed to the two journeys and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of the House.

One of the great tribes of the Arabs; it lived around the Sacred House of Allah in Makkah, undertook the service of the pilgrims, and was known for trade; it had two journeys: one in winter to Yemen, and the other in summer to Sham.
‘For the accustomed security of Quraysh, their accustomed security…’: marvel at their being accustomed to the two journeys and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of the House.
Winter: the time of cold. ‘The journey of winter and summer’: the regularity of their journey in winter to ‘Yemen’, and in summer to ‘Sham’.
Winter: the time of cold. ‘The journey of winter and summer’: the regularity of their journey in winter to ‘Yemen’, and in summer to ‘Sham’.
So let them submit and let them humble themselves.
‘The Lord of this House’: the One who raised it and its Guardian.
A relative noun for the masculine singular.
Hunger: the pain resulting from the stomach being empty of food.
He granted them safety and tranquility.
Fear: an emotion that arouses alarm in the soul due to expecting something disliked.
